lines.text: Claim Social Security at 62? Your check shrinks 30%.
lines.say: Claim Social Security at sixty-two? Your check shrinks thirty percent.

lines.text: The myth? Same check, just sooner. Here's the math.
lines.say: The myth? Same check, just sooner. Here's the math.

lines.text: Born in 1960 or later? Full retirement age is 67, and claiming at 62 pays just 70%.
lines.say: Born in nineteen sixty or later? Full retirement age is sixty-seven, and claiming at sixty-two pays just seventy percent.

lines.text: Wait until 70, and yearly credits push it to 124%.
lines.say: Wait until seventy, and yearly credits push it to one hundred twenty-four percent.
Our math: two thousand dollars at sixty-seven is fourteen hundred at sixty-two, or twenty-four hundred eighty at seventy.

lines.text: And that cut usually sticks, even after you reach 67.
lines.say: And that cut usually sticks, even after you reach sixty-seven.

lines.text: Raises still apply: the 3.6% COLA for 2027 adds about $50 to $1,400, but $72 to $2,000.
lines.say: Raises still apply: the three point six percent COLA for twenty twenty-seven adds about fifty dollars to fourteen hundred, but seventy-two to two thousand.

lines.text: Early means more checks. In our math, claiming at 67 pulls ahead around age 79.
lines.say: Early means more checks. In our math, claiming at sixty-seven pulls ahead around age seventy-nine.

lines.text: It's a trade: more checks, or bigger ones. Health and plans decide which wins.
lines.say: It's a trade: more checks, or bigger ones. Health and plans decide which wins.

post.title: Claiming Social Security at 62 can shrink your check 30%
post.ig:
Claiming Social Security at 62 can shrink your check 30%, usually for good.
Born 1960 or later? Full retirement age is 67. Claiming at 62 pays 70% of the full benefit; waiting to 70 pays 124% (SSA rules).
Our math: a $2,000 check at 67 is $1,400 at 62 or $2,480 at 70.
The cut usually sticks (rare exceptions: withdrawing within 12 months or suspending at full retirement age), but COLAs still apply: the 2027 COLA is 3.6% (SSA, Oct 14, 2026).
Our math: break-even for 62 vs 67 is around age 79.
Sources: Social Security Administration; CNBC (Oct 14, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
